overview: This is a SINGLE-TOOL depth activity. Claude Artifacts builds a working React dashboard conversationally. The wow factor is depth, not breadth — one model, multiple turns, a live interactive tool the steering committee clicks through.

steps.title: Initial dashboard build with Claude Artifacts
steps.instruction: Open a fresh Claude session with Artifacts enabled. Attach itsm_tickets_2500.xlsx. Ask Claude to build an interactive dashboard with: total tickets KPI, top problem clusters (semantic clustering), Pareto chart, severity distribution, trend by month, and application breakdown.

steps.full_prompt:
Create an interactive, filterable Problem Management dashboard from the attached itsm_tickets_2500.xlsx dataset. This is NOT a report — it is a working tool the Operations Steering Committee will click through LIVE.

Required views:
- KPI tiles: Total Tickets, Open Problems, Mean Time to Resolve (MTTR), Top Cluster Volume
- Semantic cluster analysis: group tickets by behavioural pattern (what users experienced), NOT by Category_Label. Show top 5 clusters with volume and share.
- Pareto chart: top clusters vs rest, with cumulative % line
- Severity distribution: bar chart by P1/P2/P3/P4
- Trend by month: line chart showing ticket volume over the period
- Application breakdown: which applications generate the most tickets

Required filters (must combine — region AND severity, not just one at a time):
- Date range picker
- Severity (multi-select: P1, P2, P3, P4)
- Application (dropdown)
- Assignment Group (dropdown)
- Region (if available in data)

Design principles:
- Audience: Operations Steering Committee (CIO, VP-Ops, Problem Managers). Labels in plain English.
- Color-code severity: P1=red, P2=orange, P3=yellow, P4=grey
- Interactivity: clicking a cluster or bar should drill down to show specific incident IDs, not just aggregates
- Responsive layout: works on a projected screen (landscape) and a laptop

Guardrails:
- Any derived metric (like MTTR or cluster assignment) must be labeled with its calculation method
- Pareto chart must show the cumulative % line alongside the bars
- Drill-down must reveal specific Ticket IDs, descriptions, and timestamps — not just counts

Build it now in Artifacts.

steps.title: Add filters and drill-down
steps.instruction: In the SAME Claude session, iterate conversationally. Ask Claude to add any filters that were not included in the first build. Test the drill-down: click a cluster — does it show specific ticket IDs? If not, ask Claude to add drill-down.
steps.partial_prompt:
The dashboard is missing [specific filter — fill in]. Add it.

Also: when I click on [element — fill in], I want to see [drill-down detail — fill in: specific ticket IDs, not aggregates].

[Iterate further — fill in: what else would the steering committee want to click on?]
steps.full_prompt:
The dashboard needs refinement. In the SAME session:

1. Add a Mumbai-region filter (or Region filter if the data has region columns).
2. Add a 'Show only P1/P2' quick-filter button.
3. When I click on a cluster bar in the Pareto chart, drill down to show: Ticket_ID, Description (first 80 chars), Severity, Application, Created_Date.
4. Add a 'Top 3 clusters this month vs last month' comparison view.

Keep iterating until the steering committee can answer these questions by clicking:
- 'What are the top 3 problem patterns this quarter?'
- 'Show me all P1s in the payments application.'
- 'Which cluster is growing fastest?'

steps.title: Stress-test with stakeholder questions
steps.instruction: In the SAME Claude session, test the dashboard against real stakeholder questions. Ask: 'The VP-Ops asks: which assignment group has the longest MTTR for P1s?' If the dashboard can answer it, great. If not, ask Claude to add the view.
steps.partial_prompt: A stakeholder asks: '[stakeholder question — fill in]'. Can the dashboard answer this? If not, [what to add — fill in].
steps.full_prompt:
Test the dashboard against these real steering-committee questions:

1. VP-Ops: 'Which assignment group has the longest MTTR for P1 incidents?'
2. CIO: 'Are problem volumes trending up or down over the last 3 months?'
3. Problem Manager: 'Show me tickets in the top cluster that are still open.'

For each question: can the dashboard answer it today? If yes, show me how. If no, add the view or filter needed.

Then add one more thing: a 'Download as CSV' button for the currently filtered view, so the committee can take the data offline.

steps.title: Capture the dashboard
steps.instruction: Save the Artifact URL. Take a screenshot of the dashboard in its final state. The deliverable IS the live Artifact — the steering committee will click through it at their next meeting. The DOCX just captures the URL + screenshot for the record.
